I got a notification for comment "I understand there should be multiple containers running (one for dev one for test) but should they both be exposed to the host on the same port(s) (i.e. 9092 and 9644)?", which seems to be gone now -- and I think for good reason :-)

So just for future reference: in `docker ps` output (such as `0.0.0.0:55076->9092/tcp, :::55076->9092/tcp, 0.0.0.0:55075->9644/tcp, :::55075->9644/tcp` in this case), the thing _before_ `->` is host port, and in-container port is _after_ `->`. So the dev services containers are exposed on randomly assigned ports on the host, there's no collision.
@edeandrea Here's how to test against the `main` branch: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#checking-an-issue-is-fixed-in-main

I made a few changes to the application. I realized I was using RESTEasy Reactive but my tests were using the blocking client and not the reactive one.

### Additions to `pom.xml` (replacing what was mentioned above in initial summary)
```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.assertj</groupId>
  <artifactId>assertj-core</artifactId>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
  <artifactId>quarkus-jaxrs-client-reactive</artifactId>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

### Completed `PriceResourceTests.java` (replacing what was mentioned above in initial summary)
```java
@QuarkusTest
class PriceResourceTest {
  @TestHTTPEndpoint(PriceResource.class)
  @TestHTTPResource("/stream")
  URI uri;

  @Test
  public void sseEventStream() {
    List<Double> received = ClientBuilder.newClient()
      .target(this.uri)
      .request(MediaType.SERVER_SENT_EVENTS)
      .rx(MultiInvoker.class)
      .get(Double.class)
      .select().first(3)
      .subscribe().withSubscriber(AssertSubscriber.create(3))
      .assertSubscribed()
      .awaitItems(3, Duration.ofSeconds(20))
      .assertCompleted()
      .getItems();

  assertThat(received)
    .hasSize(3)
    .allMatch(value -> (value >= 0) && (value < 100));
  }
}
```

I verified all the scenarios still do not work with Quarkus `2.1.1.Final`. I then tried the [Using Snapshots](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#using-snapshots) to use the latest Quarkus snapshot.

After re-testing, all the scenarios pass! Does this mean that this will be fixed in Quarkus `2.2`? Or will it be rolled into a Quarkus `2.1.x` maintenance release? It does not work in Quarkus `2.1.1.Final`.
